items.title: How to steal the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular in GTA 6
items.summary:
One of the cars Randy wants in GTA 6 is the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular—and don't let the name fool you, its a slick and speedy ride that'll you'll be tempted to keep for yourself.

But Randy doesn't know the locations of many of the cars on his wishlist, and can't point you to the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular: you just need to keep an eye out for it. Luckily, we spotted it ourselves, so just follow the simple steps below to find it.

Ocelot Bloodless Jugular location Head to Belville : It's a town in Leonard County, in the central eastern part of the map, a bit south of Lake Leonida and north of La Perle.

In the northern edge of Belville there's a little cluster of four homes laid out almost in an X pattern. The southernmost home of that cluster has a garage you can break into. Once you open the garage door, you'll see the white Ocelot Bloodless Jugular.

You'll need the key cloner to get in, which I assume you already have since you're doing jobs for Randy. No need to worry about the tracker , it's a standard one so it won't transmit your location to the cops. You still don't want to dawdle, because the owner of the car has a gun and he's not afraid to use it. He'll start shooting if he sees you boost the car.

Randy will pay you $10,615 for the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular. He'll pay an extra $5,000 if you bring it to him in pristine condition.

items.title: Studio founded by former Apex Legends leaders is closing without releasing a game
items.summary:
Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

Gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy said at the time. 

"That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good."

But like so many other ambitious new studios launched around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it said was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain."

(Image credit: Gravity Well) A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS ) says the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation."

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. items.title: Wizards of the Coast Sues Website That Prints Fake Magic: The Gathering Cards, Alleging Counterfeiting Operation

For as much as Magic: The Gathering has grown in popularity over the last several years, the market for proxies and counterfeits has also grown. And now, Wizards of the Coast is suing PrintMTG, alleging a counterfeiting ring for the trading card game.

Wizards of the Coast filed the lawsuit (via Aftermath ) in its home state of Washington, alleging PrintMTG "operate as a complex and sophisticated network (...) engaged in trademark infringement, counterfeiting and criminal copyright infringement on a grand scale." Wizards seeks $28.65 million in damages.

For the most part, PrintMTG was a destination for people to print proxies, or essentially fake Magic cards that could stand in for real ones, for either playtesting or trying before you buy the actual card. And, thanks to the Reserved list, there are plenty of cards that cost thousands of dollars for a legitimate copy, so it's easy to see why going to a website and spending $0.75 on a proxy version instead was a popular choice. 

In its complaint, Wizards of the Coast seems to acknowledge the purpose that proxies serve, saying "an honest proxy is a stand-in for a real card that makes no claim to authenticity by appearance or otherwise. Though proxies are prohibited in all sanctioned Magic events, Wizards recognizes that private and noncommercial proxying is a vehicle players can use to further engage with the game, not to undermine it." But, it seems PrintMTG proxies were a bit too realistic.

items.title: GTA 6 players found a '60 fps glitch', but it’s too unstable to stop me from wishing it was on PC already

Clever Grand Theft Auto 6 players have found a glitch with the Xbox version of the game that allows players to forcibly remove Rockstar's 30 fps cap. But even though people claim the game jumps up to 60 fps, the actual performance is nowhere near as smooth, according to Digital Foundry's tests.

The glitch is surprisingly simple to perform: You just need to set the console's output to 60 Hz, load GTA 6, swap the output to 120 Hz, load a different game, and then use the Quick Resume feature to go back to GTA 6. For whatever reason, this forces the game to run above 30 fps, but not by much.

In Digital Foundry's testing, GTA 6 doesn't suddenly become a buttery smooth 60 fps dream. Instead, it has an average frame rate of about 36 fps and still drops below that number during particularly intense scenes, like in city areas or when multiple cars are exploding due to rocket launcher hijinks.

The most notable improvement is lower input lag when it manages to climb up to around 40 fps, but even that has an asterisk because the frame rate varies too much for the benefits to be consistent. Unless you plan on spending your time in Leonida roleplaying as a fisherman, you're going to have a bad time.

While Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers said an official 60 fps mode for GTA 6 is too much for the current generation of consoles to handle, including the PS5 Pro, Digital Foundry theorizes that a 40 fps mode might be possible in the future.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle," Sarzynski said on Bluesky over the weekend, joking that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled."

(Image credit: Igor Sarzynski, Anna Megill on Bluesky) That news came as a surprise to Cyberpunk 2 lead writer Anna Megill, who replied with a baffled "But wait—"

Sarzynski was, of course, just goofing. But I'm sympathetic to any game dev who might be feeling an amount of apprehension about being measured against GTA 6's success, particularly when there's a genre overlap.

In Cyberpunk 2's case, however, CD Projekt is very much in its own lane: Cyberpunk is a different thematic setting, with entirely different systems and design goals. I'd hope that any reasonable person would think comparing the two is like comparing apples and oranges—particularly when the oranges reportedly had a production budget upwards of $1 billion .

In my first 30 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6 , I think I saw it rain once. And that was during a particularly gloomy main story mission where it felt like it was intentionally flipped on and not a serendipitous moment created by the game's weather system.

I was not alone in wondering what was up with the weather in Leonida. GTA 6 players have been confused by the lack of rain and fog since day one, especially after Rockstar boasted about the kind of storms and hurricanes it can create to Game Informer in September.

Apparently, the questioning was justified: The weather system was broken and should now be fixed in a new patch that went out today.

"Fixed an issue that resulted in weather not changing for extended periods," the patch notes say, confirming that, while some players witnessed changes in weather, it was not properly happening at the rate it was intended.

You don't partner with The Weather Channel to post exclusive pre-release screenshots of your game if the forecast is mostly sunny and not actually representative of Florida, the state with the most unpredictable weather in the US. GTA 6 has realistically detailed radio towers that left a TikTok guy who's worked on them in real life gobsmacked. The sun's reign is over and all the other meteorological conditions can take the spotlight. As someone who takes their time doing all the silly little daily routines in Jason and Lucia's life and abiding by traffic laws for the vibes,…

Former Dragon Age executive producer Mark Darrah has already explained how the studio was backed into a corner by EA. Escalating financial pressure led to the poor decisions and subpar games we saw ahead of BioWare's closure. But what if it had all gone differently? Despite everything, Darrah does question whether there was a way for BioWare to survive under EA.

(Image credit: EA) "BioWare's entire existence under EA—it was essentially zero sum, if somebody was getting resources it was coming at the expense of somebody else," Darrah explains. "It's almost like BioWare has run exactly the same way for its entire existence. But the external constraints were different. So in the early days when BioWare needed more people it hired more people. That's like Baldur's Gate 1, Neverwinter Nights, in the early days when we have all these different threads and branches.

items.title: Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"
items.summary:
1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project , adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many : the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

In much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise new players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered , thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the "immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the process.
items.t: Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"
